findings.advice: Resolve against advertised catalog; exact IDs take priority and a base selector must match exactly one variant. Reject unknown or ambiguous selection before prompt and after reconnect.
findings.implementation: broker.mjs resolves once, stores the exact selected ID, and rechecks fresh status before each prompt. Sequential model-only integration test covers the user's three choices.

findings.advice: Native harness model selection can call acpx/runtime setModel directly; the OpenClaw gateway exposes model via config controls.
findings.implementation: Cursor broker uses the public acpx runtime. The pinned 0.19.3 client prefers session/set_config_option for an advertised model option and supports the legacy session/set_model path.

findings.advice: Use backend-accepted controls; changing model may clamp or remove thinking support.
findings.implementation: Effort input is optional; model-only requests choose the unique advertised variant and report parsed selected/current effort. No generic thinking control is invented.

findings.advice: Drop an unsupported inherited model default, or retry OpenClaw provider-qualified model references.
findings.reason: These are OpenClaw gateway policies outside this native lane's contract. Explicit requested selection and the plugin default stay fail-closed; the task requires the three advertised Cursor base names, not provider routing.

limitations: Candidate readiness and synthetic broker tests are not installed-host execution proof. Native reload and real Cursor smoke remain gated.
